prayerExcerpt.en-US: When God called His Saints to Himself, He might, had He so pleased, have taken their bodies also; but He willed to leave them in our charge, for our help and consolation.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Quando Deus chamou os seus Santos para Si, poderia, se assim Lhe aprouvesse, ter tomado também os seus corpos; mas quis deixá-los a nosso cuidado, para nosso auxílio e consolação.

meta.face: A Gallo-Roman of about fifty-five, TALL, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fresh, ROSY complexion and a LONG, smoothly OVAL face, FULL and rounded in the rosy cheeks, with no sharp bones — a smooth, open forehead; a LONG, straight nose with a slightly RAISED, rounded tip; clear hazel eyes, a little NARROWED in a shrewd, PRUDENT, appraising look, under neatly arched brown brows; a small, composed mouth with a SHORT upper lip; a neat, softly rounded chin; a thick head of short, TIGHT, springy chestnut CURLS touched with grey, with a small tonsure; the gaze prudent and kind, toward us. Not the sharp-cheeked edmund_canterbury, the tapering, bearded hubert, the heart-shaped polycarp, the round, apple-cheeked blase or the long, fine remigius.
meta.basis: His friend St. Ouen (Audoin) describes him in the Life: 'tall with a rosy face', 'a pretty head of hair with curly locks', long fingers, 'the face of an angel and a prudent look' (Medieval Sourcebook translation); the card follows it. The reliquary and hammer are the goldsmith of the book, whose 'great delight was in making rich shrines for relics'.
